subject: literature
passage: Sabina had entered the essay contest only because her younger sister Asmita had begged her to help, and helping had somehow turned into entering. Every evening for a month they sat at the kitchen table in Pokhara, Asmita reading her sentences aloud while Sabina crossed out words and pushed the page back. When the results came, Sabina's essay had won nothing. Asmita's had placed first in the district. Sabina found, a little to her own surprise, that she did not mind at all; she had read every line of her sister's essay so many times that the prize felt partly hers.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Sabina feels that her sister's success is a shared one because of the help she gave.
choices.B: Sabina is disappointed that her own essay did not win a prize in the contest.
choices.C: Sabina regrets entering a contest that she had never wanted to take part in.
choices.D: Asmita wins the contest only because Sabina wrote most of her essay for her.

explanation.why: The text explains that Sabina entered the contest reluctantly and spent a month helping Asmita. When Asmita wins and Sabina does not, Sabina "did not mind at all," because "the prize felt partly hers." The main idea is her sense of sharing in her sister's success.
explanation.A: Correct. This captures the ending, where Sabina feels the prize is partly hers because she read and helped with every line.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says directly that Sabina "did not mind at all" that her essay won nothing.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Although Sabina entered somewhat by accident, the text never says she regrets it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Sabina crossed out words and edited, but Asmita read her own sentences aloud; the text does not say Sabina wrote the essay.
